test.name: Prioritize among multiple unresolved conflicts
test.description: Two unresolved conflicts exist simultaneously — a fact conflict (birthplace) and an identity conflict (which Patrick Flynn in 1850 is the subject). Tests whether the skill picks one conflict to work on first rather than tangling both into a single resolution.

input.delegation:
There are several unresolved conflicts in this research. Take a look and start working on whichever should come first.

projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: Should address only one conflict in this turn rather than producing tangled prose covering both
Should explain the rationale for the chosen ordering — which conflict is more foundational, blocks more downstream work, or has better evidence available to resolve
If the skill writes to the conflicts section, it should update exactly one conflict's analysis fields and leave the other untouched

Outcome: the pass may take either conflict first. If it works c_002, c_002 must end resolved with preferred_assertion_id a_001. Ruling (senior genealogist, #4326): c_002 resolves, preferred_assertion_id a_001. Patrick is in Thomas Flynn's household in 1850 (age 5) and 1860 (age 15), and the 1908 certificate names Thomas Flynn as father through a different informant (the son-in-law). Those agree. The rival Patrick in household 197 appears only in the conflict's description, with no record of his own, so nothing on file supports him. An analysis that calls the father's name circular and defers is the wrong outcome.
